points.text: In-sample Sharpe 0.53 on JPM bollinger reversion. Short-term mean reversion on daily bars is among the most published anomalies in equities; a 0.53 in-sample Sharpe after the desk's own selection is weak evidence of a surviving edge — the publication decay on daily MR is well documented.

55 trades over 11 years (~5/yr) for a 'short-term' mean-reversion system is slow — true short-term MR trades weekly or more. The holding periods here bleed into swing territory, where the MR rationale (overnight reversal, bid-ask bounce) no longer applies.

Daily timeframe on JPM (deep liquidity): 5 bps/side is conservative and the cost-sensitivity curve should be flat. Unlike MR-5M, costs are unlikely to be the executioner here — the verdict will come from the DSR and benchmark gates instead.

Same DSR arithmetic as the trend ideas: 0.53 in-sample at n=70 is far below the null's expected best. The DSR gate will almost surely fail — and that is the gate doing its job against a mined MR parameter.

JPM buy-and-hold over 2015-2026 was strong (banks' post-2016 run). The Tier-1 benchmark gate needs excess vs holding JPM — a mean-reversion system that underperforms its own underlying's drift is a hard sell.
